source.title: From Theft to Bomb-Making: The Ripple Effect of Unlearning in Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks
source.authors: Zhe-Xin Zhang; Junxiao Yang; Yi-Da Lu; Pei Ke; Shiyao Cui; Chujie Zheng; Hong-Ning Wang; Min-Lie Huang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It includes the main sections and appendices; no relevant portion appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests unlearning methods against jailbreak prompts and reports when they do and do not elicit harmful responses after unlearning. Its results challenge a broad claim that prompt attacks generally recover the targeted behavior, while showing residual failures, especially with PAIR.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ASR outcomes for raw harmful prompts, manual jailbreaks, adaptive attacks and prefilling after unlearning. These count as tests of prompting-based recovery, not tests of rephrasing alone. Hidden-state visualizations and token probabilities are reported, but there is no activation-direction ablation, quantization attack or relearning attack. Values used only to select settings are not included.
record.test_reason: This is a new setting: harmful-response unlearning as a jailbreak defense on HarmBench. After unlearning (Safe Unlearning, RMU, Circuit Breaker, small-beta DPO) it reports attack success rates (ASR) under manual, GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR and prefilling attacks, which bears on whether prompting recovers unlearned content (E). It also reports raw ASR plus MTBench/MMLU, which bear on A. It is not T5: the paper argues for unlearning's generalization and makes no argument against a version. No fine-tuning, ablation or quantization attack is run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that unlearning harmful responses for 100 HarmBench questions also suppresses harmful output on unseen questions under most jailbreaks (a ripple effect), while keeping general performance. They argue that sufficient unlearning (high PPL) is what separates these methods from SFT. They attribute PAIR's residual success to dispersed, subtle or policy-dependent harms, not to retained knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates several harmful-knowledge defenses, including RMU and Circuit Breaker, and introduces Safe Unlearning as an NPO-based extension with rejection and maintaining losses. It tests jailbreak defense on HarmBench rather than fine-tuning, activation ablation or quantization as recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by attack method: PAIR has substantially higher residual ASR than most tested methods. DPO outcomes also vary with beta. The paper notes that unlearning degree varies slightly across models and that certain dispersed, subtle or context-dependent harms are harder to unlearn.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning sharply raises perplexity on constructed harmful responses, including responses to OOD questions never in the forget set (e.g., Llama 1.71 to 5.89e5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-response unlearning lowers likelihood of unseen harmful completions (a ripple effect).

record.problems: The main evaluation uses two representative chat models, and the paper says additional models and attack methods remain untested. It does not report uncertainty estimates. ASR is judged using HarmBench-Llama-2-13b-cls, whose accuracy is reported as approximately 94.5% in its original study. No model that never had the targeted knowledge is used as a comparator. The paper notes that some harmful categories are dispersed, subtle or policy-dependent and are difficult to unlearn.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, most individual ASR results for non-PAIR methods other than Safe Unlearning were omitted. The retained comparator rows cover PAIR across the methods and models because the paper highlights its residual success. Other omitted results are in Tables 1 and 2; Qwen scale results are in Table 7; GPTFuzzer and DRA results are in Table 9.

untested.parts: Targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance (the measure is harmful-generation ASR, not QA accuracy); no comparison with a never-trained model; recovery by fine-tuning, ablation or quantization.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All: no direction ablation. The t-SNE and token-probability analyses do not test block-versus-delete.
Other languages, in-context information, and plain rephrasing as a separate condition.
Safe Unlearning is shown resisting prompting attacks only, not fine-tuning, ablation or quantization attacks.

missing.what: XSTest over-refusal after Safe Unlearning (Llama 29.6 vs 4.0; Mistral 7.2 vs 2.8), a general-ability cost.
Related benign knowledge retained in 97% (Llama) and 99% (Mistral) of 100 related benign questions.
GCG attack on Llama + Safe Unlearning across 16 AIR-Bench categories, with failures in subtle and policy-dependent categories (figure only, no numbers in the text).

record.verdict_notes: The record's version codes V1/V5 were invalid. Raw-prompt and capability rows are remapped to A, attack rows to E, and SFT and DPO1 comparators to none. ID questions are the forget set itself; OOD results reflect generalization, not targeted forgetting. The 'knowledge' here is harmful-response generation judged by a classifier (about 94.5% accuracy), not factual QA accuracy as in WMDP or Harry Potter. Decoding is greedy, with no uncertainty reported. Tranche changed from T5 to T3.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports ASR and general benchmarks, not targeted-knowledge accuracy against an explicit chance level. It does not compare with a model that never had the knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation is performed, and the analyses do not establish that the methods block access rather than delete knowledge.
The study tests several jailbreak strategies and prefilling, but not rephrasing in isolation, other languages, or in-context information as separate attack conditions.
The study tests defenses against jailbreak attacks, not resistance to the fine-tuning, activation-ablation or quantization attacks named in the claim.

relation.reason: Reports ASR under several attacks plus general performance, which bears on versions A and E.

tranche.reason: New setting (harmful-response unlearning as a jailbreak defense) with results that bear on A and E. The reader's T5 is not needed.

source_check.notes: All 25 rows match Tables 1-2. Target is harmful-response ASR, not knowledge accuracy; No Defense is fine-tuned on the retain set, and PPL is measured only without attacks. No row or verdict covers RMU on Mistral under GCG/AutoDAN/manual (9.7-23.0), a partial recovery bearing on E. Appendix D adds Qwen2.5-3B/14B/32B.

statements.correction: 2407.02855 runs manual, AutoDAN, GCG, PAIR and prefilling attacks (Tables 1-2), plus GPTFuzzer and DRA (Table 9), on the unlearned models. Safe Unlearning ASR stays at 0-5 under all of these except PAIR (14-26) and DRA (7-14). Appendix D adds Qwen2.5-3B/14B/32B as a third family.
statements.problem: The ASR and MMLU numbers match Tables 1-2. But the conditions say REVS is the only study here that runs an attack, and 2407.02855 also attacks its unlearned models. 'Two families' leaves out the appendix Qwen2.5 runs.

statements.correction: 2407.02855, Safe Unlearning, both models, ID and OOD: GCG 2.0-5.0, AutoDAN 1.0-4.0, PAIR 14.0-26.0 (No Defense 55-96). GCG/AutoDAN partly succeed only against RMU on Mistral (12.0-23.0) and against Circuit Breaker AutoDAN on Mistral (8.0-10.0). The study reports PPL on harmful responses as its measure of knowledge removal: Safe Unlearning 5.89e5-1.73e6 vs No Defense 1.71-1.96, measured without attacks.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the lead says optimized or iterative attacks bring part of it back. In this study the optimized GCG and AutoDAN stay at 0-5 against Safe Unlearning; only PAIR partly recovers. The conditions' 'no knowledge probe' also leaves out the study's PPL measure.

statements.correction: Safe Unlearning: manual/AutoDAN/GCG/prefilling ASR 0-5 (both models, ID and OOD). Under manual/AutoDAN/GCG, RMU on Mistral gives 9.7-23.0 and Circuit Breaker on Mistral up to 10.0. PAIR gives 7-26 for Safe Unlearning, Circuit Breaker, DPO2 and RMU on Llama, and 42-52 for RMU on Mistral.
statements.problem: The 0-5 range for manual/AutoDAN/GCG/prefilling holds for Safe Unlearning only, but the sentence applies it to harmful-behaviour unlearning in general. The PAIR clause covers several methods, including RMU.

statements.correction: 2407.02855 reports ASR (HarmBench-Llama-2-13b-cls) and PPL on harmful responses generated by Llama-3-8B-Lexi-Uncensored: No Defense 1.71-1.96, Safe Unlearning 5.89e5-1.73e6, ID and OOD, without attacks. It has no accuracy-style knowledge test.
statements.problem: The main point stands: the target is harmful output, not targeted-knowledge accuracy. But 'no knowledge probe' is inexact: the authors use PPL on constructed harmful responses as their measure of harmful-knowledge removal.

statements.correction: Safe Unlearning, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, ID: manual 1.5, AutoDAN 1.0, GCG 2.0, PAIR 17.0, prefilling 0 (No Defense 73.2-96.0). Only PAIR (iterative) recovers more than the fixed prompts.
